interaction.text: A climbing vine studded with tiny star-shaped blossoms. Doesn't seem to be anything but pretty.
A cluster of pale blue flowers, nodding in whatever breeze makes it this deep into the swamp.
Broad-leafed and unbothered, growing in the shade of taller things. If it has a name, nobody's bothered to use it.
A cheerful little patch of yellow starbursts, entirely unconnected to the one you're actually looking for.
More of the same purple spikes as everywhere else nearby. The herbalist clearly isn't precious about spacing.
A tangle of green climbing along the fence line, more interested in the sunlight than in being useful to you.
A stand of deep pink blossoms, growing thick along the garden path. Smells faintly of honey.
A patch of orange-flecked ground cover, low and unremarkable, tucked near the treeline.
A cluster of rocks half-submerged at the pond's edge, a single red flower somehow rooted between them.
The same little rockery, from a slightly different angle. Still just rocks.
A single purple bloom growing stubbornly out of a crack near the water's edge.

_incomplete: Converted from herbalist_hut_exterior.tmj/tmx (INFINITE/CHUNKED Tiled format), merged all chunks into a dense 48x32 grid with computed origin offset (tile-space [-32, -32]). Collision built from the union of the two authored 'walkable area'/'walkable 2' polygon objects (rasterized, inside = walkable), not inferred from any tile footprint. Spawn taken from the 'player entrance' point object. The 'herbalist hut entrance' rectangle already lands on walkable tiles inside the polygon, no threshold carving was needed. targetX/targetY on exit_swamp_to_hut are placeholders (null) pending the interior's own entrance/exit tile, filled in during the paired interior conversion in this same delivery. 16 point objects on the 'PLANTS' layer were NOT wired as interactive objects, since which plant is which, and the reference-chart/plant-matching mechanic itself, is still an open design question (see MEANS_AND_OPPORTUNITY-era house style: don't invent unconfirmed content). Their raw tile coordinates are preserved verbatim in the top-level 'plantMarkers' array for whoever designs that puzzle next. Layer kind assignments (floor vs sorted) follow the established precedent from estate.json's own Trees/Bushes/Flowers/Birds layers, not verified in-browser yet.
